strings.d1.s0.name: Christ the Redeemer Corcovado
strings.d1.s0.tips: The cog train from Cosme Velho (timed online tickets, first departure 08:00, about 100 BRL) climbs through Tijuca Forest. The 38 m Christ is quiet in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Parque Lage
strings.d1.s1.tips: A mansion and pool courtyard beneath Corcovado, set in the forest. It was a location for a Snoop Dogg video.
strings.d1.s2.name: Santa Teresa Bar do Mineiro
strings.d1.s2.tips: A bohemian hilltop neighbourhood. Try feijoada (Saturday) and bolinho (fried snack), and ride the tram (bonde).
strings.d1.s3.name: Escadaria Selarón
strings.d1.s3.tips: 2,000 tiled steps by a Chilean artist, leading down to Lapa. There are Turkish tiles among them too.
strings.d1.s4.name: Arcos da Lapa
strings.d1.s4.tips: An aqueduct from 1750. Samba at night (Fridays at Rio Scenarium).
strings.d1.b0.name: Aprazível Santa Teresa
strings.d1.b0.tips: A forest restaurant with treehouse-style dining. Views over Guanabara Bay; book ahead.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museu Chácara do Céu
strings.d1.b1.tips: A modern art villa in Santa Teresa, with views.
strings.d2.s0.name: Copacabana Beach
strings.d2.s0.tips: Winter (Jun-Sep) is sunny at 24°C, which locals say is the best season. The sea is 22°C.
strings.d2.s1.name: Arpoador Rock
strings.d2.s1.tips: A rock between Copacabana and Ipanema, with surfers and views of Dois Irmãos.
strings.d2.s2.name: Ipanema Beach Posto 9
strings.d2.s2.tips: The beach of The Girl from Ipanema. Vendors sell biscoito Globo (light crunchy biscuits) and mate; Posto 9 has a young crowd.
strings.d2.s3.name: Garota de Ipanema Bar
strings.d2.s3.tips: The bar where the song was written. Order picanha (grilled beef) and chope (draught beer).
strings.d2.s4.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
strings.d2.s4.tips: A two-stage cable car (Urca 220 m, Sugarloaf 396 m). Go for sunset and the city lights at night; timed online tickets.
strings.d2.b0.name: Bar Urca
strings.d2.b0.tips: Beer and pastel (fried pastry) on the Urca sea wall. A local classic, before the cable car.
strings.d2.b1.name: Forte de Copacabana
strings.d2.b1.tips: A fort at the end of the beach, with the Confeitaria Colombo café. An alternative to Arpoador.
strings.d3.s0.name: Museum of Tomorrow
strings.d3.s0.tips: Calatrava's Museum of Tomorrow on the Porto Maravilha waterfront. Free on Tuesdays.
strings.d3.s1.name: Monastery of São Bento
strings.d3.s1.tips: A gold-covered Baroque monastery from 1590. Gregorian mass on Sundays at 10:00.
strings.d3.s2.name: Confeitaria Colombo
strings.d3.s2.tips: A Belle Époque pastry shop from 1894. Mirrored hall, pastel de nata and salgados (savoury snacks).
strings.d3.s3.name: Real Gabinete Português de Leitura
strings.d3.s3.tips: One of the world's most beautiful libraries (Neo-Manueline style). Free.
strings.d3.s4.name: Pedra do Sal
strings.d3.s4.tips: The rock where samba was born. Street roda (samba circle) on Mondays and Fridays; try a caipirinha.
strings.d3.b0.name: Rio Scenarium
strings.d3.b0.tips: A three-storey samba house packed with antiques. Fridays and Saturdays.
strings.d3.b1.name: Theatro Municipal
strings.d3.b1.tips: A replica of the Paris Opera. Check tour times.
strings.d4.s0.name: Pedra Bonita Trail
strings.d4.s0.tips: 693 m in Tijuca. An easy 40-minute climb to a hang-gliding ramp, with views of Pedra da Gávea and São Conrado.
strings.d4.s1.name: Cascatinha Taunay Tijuca Forest
strings.d4.s1.tips: A 30 m waterfall in the world's largest urban forest. Look out for monkeys; take an Uber or taxi.
strings.d4.s2.name: Dona Marta Viewpoint
strings.d4.s2.tips: The most famous frame of Christ, Sugarloaf and the bay. A Michael Jackson video was shot here.
strings.d4.s3.name: Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden
strings.d4.s3.tips: A botanical garden from 1808. A 134 m avenue of imperial palms and Vitória Régia giant water lilies.
strings.d4.s4.name: Braseiro da Gávea
strings.d4.s4.tips: Picanha and chope in Gávea. A meat restaurant popular with locals.
strings.d4.b0.name: Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas Cycling
strings.d4.b0.tips: A 7.5 km loop around the lagoon, with boats. An alternative to the botanical garden.
strings.d4.b1.name: Bar Lagoa
strings.d4.b1.tips: A German-Brazilian bar on the lagoon shore, open since 1934.
strings.d5.s0.name: Conceição de Jacareí Ilha Grande Boat
strings.d5.s0.tips: A 2.5-hour transfer from Rio plus a 20-minute boat ride (tour about 250 BRL). A car-free forest island.
strings.d5.s1.name: Vila do Abraão
strings.d5.s1.tips: The island's village, with sandy streets and a church.
strings.d5.s2.name: Lopes Mendes Beach
strings.d5.s2.tips: One of Brazil's most beautiful beaches. Take a boat plus a 20-minute forest walk; white sand and bodyboarding.
strings.d5.s3.name: Lua e Mar Beach Tavern Abraão
strings.d5.s3.tips: Moqueca (fish stew) and caipirinha. The return boat leaves at 16:30.
strings.d5.b0.name: Lagoa Azul Snorkelling Tour
strings.d5.b0.tips: A boat tour to the Blue Lagoon with turtles and fish. An alternative to Lopes Mendes.
strings.d5.b1.name: Praia do Abraãozinho Kiosk
strings.d5.b1.tips: A cove beach next to the village.
strings.d6.s0.name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: Niemeyer's flying saucer. The ferry takes 20 minutes (from Praça XV), and it has the best view of the Rio skyline.
strings.d6.s1.name: Parque da Cidade Niterói
strings.d6.s1.tips: A hilltop in Niterói with a bay panorama stretching to Christ the Redeemer, and hang-gliding.
strings.d6.s2.name: Itacoatiara Beach
strings.d6.s2.tips: Watch the winter surf. Beach kiosks.
strings.d6.s3.name: Mercado São Pedro Niterói
strings.d6.s3.tips: Upstairs restaurants above the fish market. Fried fish.
strings.d6.s4.name: Maracanã Stadium Tour
strings.d6.s4.tips: The world's legendary stadium. Take a tour or catch a match (Flamengo or Fluminense, a real experience!); get there by metro.
strings.d6.b0.name: Flamengo Match Maracanã
strings.d6.b0.tips: A match-day stand. The best Rio experience; buy tickets online.
strings.d6.b1.name: Skunna Niterói
strings.d6.b1.tips: A seafront restaurant in Niterói, with views.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mirante do Leblon
strings.d7.s0.tips: A lookout at the end of Leblon, with views of the Ipanema and Leblon beaches and Dois Irmãos.
strings.d7.s1.name: Leblon Beach Morning
strings.d7.s1.tips: Rio's most elegant beach. Have coconut water (água de coco).
strings.d7.s2.name: Talho Capixaba Leblon
strings.d7.s2.tips: A Leblon bakery-deli breakfast. Pão de queijo (cheese bread) for your farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Feira Hippie Ipanema
strings.d7.s3.tips: A handicrafts market on Sundays at Praça General Osório (on other days, visit a Havaianas store).
strings.d7.s4.name: Galeão Airport Uber
strings.d7.b0.name: Bibi Sucos Leblon
strings.d7.b0.tips: A cult spot for açaí and fruit juice.
strings.d7.b1.name: Museu Casa do Pontal
strings.note0: The metro (Zona Sul to Centro) is safe and clean; Uber and 99 are cheap; the Niterói ferry leaves from Praça XV. Galeão takes 45-60 minutes; Santos Dumont is in the city.
strings.note1: December to March is summer: 35-40°C, humid and rainy. Carnival falls in February or March (hotels cost three times as much, with blocos street parties). On New Year's Eve, 2 million people dress in white on Copacabana.
strings.note2: SAFETY: Don't show your phone on the street, don't leave belongings on the beach (swim one at a time), don't walk on the seafront at night, and don't enter a favela without a guide. Zona Sul (Ipanema, Leblon, Copacabana) is comfortable by day.
strings.note3: Corcovado train 100 BRL, Sugarloaf 180, Maracanã 60; por quilo (pay-by-weight) restaurant 40-60, chope 12, caipirinha 20; 10% service charge is added to the bill. Cards are accepted everywhere, and Pix works too.
strings.note4: Christ the Redeemer at 08:00 (cloud rolls in after noon), Sugarloaf at sunset; take the Ilha Grande tour early; Pedra Bonita in the morning.
strings.note5: Feijoada on Saturday, açaí, pão de queijo, moqueca, picanha; Globo biscuits on the beach.
